## Overview
Follow-up of #57549

Enable EPLB for DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 DSpark drafts when their expert topology differs from the target model.
This PR covers DSpark’s draft model loader.
Related: [#59611](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59611) fixes redundant expert loading in the target model. 


## Claims

- Register supported DSpark draft MoE models with the target’s EPLB state.
- Allow target and draft models to have different expert counts and topologies. Reduce load statistics for all registered models in one collective, including when their physical expert counts differ.
- Include redundant expert slots in the V4.1 DSpark fused-MoE weight mapping.

## Validation
- CPU-runnable pytest subset:.
- Add coverage for heterogeneous topology handling, EPLB registration, and DSpark redundant-slot mapping.

### GSM8K validation.

server:
```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --served-model-name nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb \
  --eplb-config '{"num_redundant_experts":8,"draft_num_redundant_experts":8, "step_interval":100,"log_balancedness":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
```

client:
```
python \
  tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --max-tokens 256 \
  --host http://127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --temperature 0.0 \
  --seed 42 \
```

Result. Accuracy: 0.890


Logs:
```
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2822063) INFO 10-14 18:33:21 [eplb_state.py:641] EPLB step: 79 for model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 (draft): avg_tokens=4500.00, max_tokens=6896, balancedness=0.6526, steps until the next rearrangement: 21
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2822063) INFO 10-14 18:33:21 [eplb_state.py:641] EPLB step: 79 for model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4: avg_tokens=238800.00, max_tokens=354552, balancedness=0.6735, steps until the next rearrangement: 21
```

Both models (target and draft) are involved in eplb rearrangement.


## Details

The target and DSpark draft can have different routed and physical expert counts. EPLB state now keeps topology-dependent counts per registered model and handles load-stat reductions when models have different physical expert dimensions.

DSpark’s custom weight loader is a separate call path from the target model’s `get_expert_mapping`. Since DSpark is now registered with EPLB, its redundant physical slots must also receive the replicated expert weights. #59611 addresses the target model’s mapping; end-to-end use with redundant experts requires that fix as well.

Thanks a lot @ilmarkov! Draft EPLB is a key piece of our [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D + Wide-EP blog](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-23-deepseek-v41-flash-pd-wide-ep). On GB300 NVL72 at DEP32, it raises the DSpark draft's balancedness from 0.21 to 0.89 and cuts the draft's MegaMoE time from 0.92 to 0.55 ms per step (Figure 6). That also answers the earlier question about a measurable gain. Really appreciate this work.

Taking `num_replicas`/`num_groups` per model in `rearrange()` and loading every local replica in the DSpark loaders both look right to me. I'm requesting changes mainly for item 1; details are inline:

1. V4.1 DSpark + EPLB no longer starts when EP is not a power of two. I suggest letting the draft's redundant expert count be set separately.
2. The heterogeneous `rearrange()` path has no test.
3. The test diff is about 6x the code diff, and AGENTS.md asks to cut scope when the test diff dwarfs the change. I've marked the tests I think can go.
4. Two small simplifications in `eplb_state.py`.

Adding V4.1 here makes the draft inherit the target's `enable_eplb` and `num_redundant_experts`. V4.1-Flash has 384 target and 128 draft routed experts, so `(384 + R) % EP == 0` and `(128 + R) % EP == 0` can both hold only when EP divides 256. When EP is not a power of two (12/24/48/72), building the draft now raises `ValueError: EPLB currently only supports even distribution of experts across ranks` (`fused_moe/layer.py`), and no choice of `R` avoids it. On main the draft was built with EPLB off and `R=0`, so these configurations started. MegaMoE already rejected these EP sizes on main, so only the default FusedMoE path regresses.

Since `EplbState` now keeps the topology per model, could the draft's redundant expert count be set on its own? For example, an optional draft override next to `draft_tensor_parallel_size` that `_get_dspark_parallel_config` applies, defaulting to the target's `R`. A config-time check of `(dspark_n_routed_experts + R_draft) % EP` that points at that option would turn this error into something users can act on. The new docs section should mention it too.

- Reuse the eval check from #59611. Thanks for the quick update, @ilmarkov! `draft_num_redundant_experts`, the heterogeneous `rearrange()` test and the flattened `_allreduce_list` address my earlier points.

A few follow-ups on the new head:

1. A design question on the default for `draft_num_redundant_experts`, and on a draft-only EPLB off switch.
2. Two of the new tests will fail in CI: the rearrange test on the single-GPU H200 MIG job, and the V4.1 DSpark config test on the MI355 Engine Core job.
3. The DSpark draft validation derives the EP size from the draft TP, while the draft's MoE layers use the global EP group.
4. A few small cleanups.

Something I'd like to discuss: is inheriting the target's count the right default when the draft has a different number of routed experts?

- When the counts match (MTP drafts, V4 DSpark), inheriting is exactly right, and it is what main enforces today via `assert_confs_equal`.
- When they differ (V4.1 DSpark: 384 vs 128), the target's count was chosen for 384 experts, and whether it also works for 128 is arithmetic coincidence: `384 + R` and `128 + R` are both divisible by EP only when EP divides 256. `R = EP` happens to work at DEP16/DEP32, while EP=12/24/36 fail. `0` isn't a natural default either, since it still needs `128 % EP == 0`.

What do you think about splitting by topology: keep inheriting when the draft and target have the same routed-expert count, and require an explicit `draft_num_redundant_experts` when they differ? The error already reports the lowest valid count. Requiring it for every draft would break existing MTP + EPLB setups, which seems unnecessary.

Related: there is currently no way to keep EPLB on for the target but off for the draft (`draft_num_redundant_experts=0` still enables draft EPLB). Would you be open to an explicit switch for that, e.g. to A/B the draft separately or to fall back when draft EPLB doesn't pay off for a workload?

This validates against an EP size of `draft_tp * pcp * dp`, but the draft's MoE layers don't use the draft TP for EP. `DeepseekV4MoE` sizes itself from `get_ep_group()`, and `FusedMoE` uses the global TP/DP/PCP groups, so the draft's runtime EP is always the target's. The two diverge with `draft_tensor_parallel_size=1`, which `_verify_and_get_draft_tp` allows:

detail.body:
## Overview
Follow-up of #57549

Enable EPLB for DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 DSpark drafts when their expert topology differs from the target model.
This PR covers DSpark’s draft model loader.
Related: [#59611](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59611) fixes redundant expert loading in the target model. 


## Claims

- Register supported DSpark draft MoE models with the target’s EPLB state.
- Allow target and draft models to have different expert counts and topologies. Reduce load statistics for all registered models in one collective, including when their physical expert counts differ.
- Include redundant expert slots in the V4.1 DSpark fused-MoE weight mapping.

## Validation
- CPU-runnable pytest subset:.
- Add coverage for heterogeneous topology handling, EPLB registration, and DSpark redundant-slot mapping.

### GSM8K validation.

server:
```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --served-model-name nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb \
  --eplb-config '{"num_redundant_experts":8,"draft_num_redundant_experts":8, "step_interval":100,"log_balancedness":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
```

client:
```
python \
  tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --max-tokens 256 \
  --host http://127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --temperature 0.0 \
  --seed 42 \
```

Result. Accuracy: 0.890


Logs:
```
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2822063) INFO 10-14 18:33:21 [eplb_state.py:641] EPLB step: 79 for model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 (draft): avg_tokens=4500.00, max_tokens=6896, balancedness=0.6526, steps until the next rearrangement: 21
(Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=2822063) INFO 10-14 18:33:21 [eplb_state.py:641] EPLB step: 79 for model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4: avg_tokens=238800.00, max_tokens=354552, balancedness=0.6735, steps until the next rearrangement: 21
```

Both models (target and draft) are involved in eplb rearrangement.


## Details

The target and DSpark draft can have different routed and physical expert counts. EPLB state now keeps topology-dependent counts per registered model and handles load-stat reductions when models have different physical expert dimensions.

DSpark’s custom weight loader is a separate call path from the target model’s `get_expert_mapping`. Since DSpark is now registered with EPLB, its redundant physical slots must also receive the replicated expert weights. #59611 addresses the target model’s mapping; end-to-end use with redundant experts requires that fix as well.

Adding V4.1 here makes the draft inherit the target's `enable_eplb` and `num_redundant_experts`. V4.1-Flash has 384 target and 128 draft routed experts, so `(384 + R) % EP == 0` and `(128 + R) % EP == 0` can both hold only when EP divides 256. When EP is not a power of two (12/24/48/72), building the draft now raises `ValueError: EPLB currently only supports even distribution of experts across ranks` (`fused_moe/layer.py`), and no choice of `R` avoids it. On main the draft was built with EPLB off and `R=0`, so these configurations started. MegaMoE already rejected these EP sizes on main, so only the default FusedMoE path regresses.

Since `EplbState` now keeps the topology per model, could the draft's redundant expert count be set on its own? For example, an optional draft override next to `draft_tensor_parallel_size` that `_get_dspark_parallel_config` applies, defaulting to the target's `R`. A config-time check of `(dspark_n_routed_experts + R_draft) % EP` that points at that option would turn this error into something users can act on. The new docs section should mention it too.

Something I'd like to discuss: is inheriting the target's count the right default when the draft has a different number of routed experts?

- When the counts match (MTP drafts, V4 DSpark), inheriting is exactly right, and it is what main enforces today via `assert_confs_equal`.
- When they differ (V4.1 DSpark: 384 vs 128), the target's count was chosen for 384 experts, and whether it also works for 128 is arithmetic coincidence: `384 + R` and `128 + R` are both divisible by EP only when EP divides 256. `R = EP` happens to work at DEP16/DEP32, while EP=12/24/36 fail. `0` isn't a natural default either, since it still needs `128 % EP == 0`.

What do you think about splitting by topology: keep inheriting when the draft and target have the same routed-expert count, and require an explicit `draft_num_redundant_experts` when they differ? The error already reports the lowest valid count. Requiring it for every draft would break existing MTP + EPLB setups, which seems unnecessary.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks a lot @ilmarkov! Draft EPLB is a key piece of our [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D + Wide-EP blog](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-23-deepseek-v41-flash-pd-wide-ep). On GB300 NVL72 at DEP32, it raises the DSpark draft's balancedness from 0.21 to 0.89 and cuts the draft's MegaMoE time from 0.92 to 0.55 ms per step (Figure 6). That also answers the earlier question about a measurable gain. Really appreciate this work.

Taking `num_replicas`/`num_groups` per model in `rearrange()` and loading every local replica in the DSpark loaders both look right to me. I'm requesting changes mainly for item 1; details are inline:

1. V4.1 DSpark + EPLB no longer starts when EP is not a power of two. I suggest letting the draft's redundant expert count be set separately.
2. The heterogeneous `rearrange()` path has no test.
3. The test diff is about 6x the code diff, and AGENTS.md asks to cut scope when the test diff dwarfs the change. I've marked the tests I think can go.
4. Two small simplifications in `eplb_state.py`.

Thanks for the quick update, @ilmarkov! `draft_num_redundant_experts`, the heterogeneous `rearrange()` test and the flattened `_allreduce_list` address my earlier points.

A few follow-ups on the new head:

1. A design question on the default for `draft_num_redundant_experts`, and on a draft-only EPLB off switch.
2. Two of the new tests will fail in CI: the rearrange test on the single-GPU H200 MIG job, and the V4.1 DSpark config test on the MI355 Engine Core job.
3. The DSpark draft validation derives the EP size from the draft TP, while the draft's MoE layers use the global EP group.
4. A few small cleanups.
